QF.id: AIFM Modern Portfolio Theory and Capital Market Theory_3

question.text: The portfolio research desk at Kaveri Capital AIF is forecasting the expected return on an unlisted stock that the fund may acquire via a secondary. The probability distribution of returns is: Boom (prob 0.30) returns 28%; Normal (prob 0.50) returns 12%; Recession (prob 0.20) returns -6%. What is the ex-ante expected rate of return?

explanation.text: The Logic: Expected return = Σ Pi*Ri = (0.30 × 28%) + (0.50 × 12%) + (0.20 × -6%) = 8.40% + 6.00% - 1.20% = 13.20%. This is an ex-ante (forward-looking) return, as distinct from ex-post (historical) returns. The Trap: 11.4% drops the probability weights and averages only two states. 14.6% double-counts the boom probability. 12.0% is simply the 'Normal' state return and ignores the distribution. Cross-Exam Context: XXI-B Portfolio Managers and XV Research Analyst also test this probability-weighted expected-return calculation. IA L1 (X-A) limits it to two states.
